bundle.author: datawithtristan
bundle.title: [DATA-2736] Add the Win election frame and race field
bundle.body:
## What changed

Adds the warehouse layer for the post-election Win report, so the report refreshes on its own once Nov 3 results land.

- **`win_election_frame`** (mart): one row per Win candidate with a 2026 race. Covers who they are, how the race went, and what they did in the product before it. Behavior is cut off at `candidacy_race_date`, which is the primary date for a primary loser. Result columns stay null until a result is matched, so the same rows work before, during and after results come in.
- **`win_race_field`** (mart): every candidate in every 2026 race where a Win user ran, users and others. Used to compare Win users with their own field and against the odds each race gave (`baseline_win_chance` = seats ÷ candidates).
- **`user_feature_use`** / **`int__user_feature_use`**: when each user first and last used each Win feature. Which events count as a feature lives in the new **`win_feature_events`** seed, so every analysis reads the same definition. Impersonated and machine-emitted events are excluded.
- **`int__user_outreach_audiences`** + **`stg_airbyte_source__gp_api_db_voter_file_filter`**: the saved audience behind each outreach send, with how many demographic families it narrows on. Ticking every option in a family counts as no filter.
- **`int__user_candidacy_profile`**: new `candidacy_race_date`, which flows through to `user_journey`.

## Why it is shaped this way

- **Contested status comes from the race's candidate list where civics has it, with the journey's opponent count as the fallback.** The journey's count misses real opponents in some races. `contest_source` records which source was used.
- **Seats are at least the number of winners**, because some multi-seat races are recorded with one seat.
- **A recorded loss means a contest** even when civics lacks the opponents. In those races `baseline_win_chance` is null rather than a false sure win.
- **Dates, not flags, in feature use.** Each analysis applies its own cutoff to the same rows.

## Verification (dev, `private_tristan`, 2026-10-29)

`dbt build` on all changed models plus `user_journey`, `user_journey_events` and the singular journey tests: PASS=48, ERROR=0.

| Table | Rows | Note |
|---|---|---|
| win_election_frame | 12,670 | 1,438 with a result so far |
| win_race_field | 11,103 | 4,368 Win-user rows; 10,212 contested; 63 with a null baseline |
| user_feature_use | 17,989 | 7,751 users |
| int__user_outreach_audiences | 7,673 | 1,515 users |

Contest source in the frame: 3,595 from the race list, 732 from the journey, 8,343 unknown (no civics match yet).

On races already decided, uncontested candidates are expected to win 100% and won 98.6%. Before the seat and opponent fixes, the numbers were 79% expected and 82% actual.

## Operational notes

- New models carry no excluded tags, so the 12-hour scheduled build picks them up.
- `user_journey` gains one column. If a scheduled run started on an older commit is in flight at merge, it can rebuild `user_journey` without the column. Re-check prod after that run ends.
- In dev, the two `user_journey` singular tests fail if your dev schema holds stale copies of `int__user_revenue_profile` or `user_journey_events`. That's not caused by this change; drop or rebuild those copies.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Large new mart logic and election-anchored cutoffs affect reported win/usage metrics; `user_journey` must expose `candidacy_race_date` for `win_election_frame` to build, and a mid-merge scheduled run could briefly rebuild journey without the new column.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds the **dbt layer for the 2026 Win post-election report**: one mart row per candidate with race context, outcome flags, and **product behavior capped at `race_date`** (primary date when they lost in the primary, otherwise the anchor election date).
> 
> **`candidacy_race_date`** is computed on `int__user_candidacy_profile` so primary losers are not credited with activity after they were eliminated; `win_election_frame` uses it for every pre-race feature, outreach, activity, and HubSpot touch measure.
> 
> New **shared building blocks**: `win_feature_events` seed plus `int__user_feature_use` / `user_feature_use` (first/last use and use days from Amplitude, excluding impersonation and machine events); **`gp_api_db_voter_file_filter` staging** with demographic “narrowing” dimension counts; **`int__user_outreach_audiences`** for sends with saved audiences. **`win_race_field`** lists every candidacy-stage in 2026 races where a Win user ran (contested logic, seats vs winners, **`baseline_win_chance`**) so the frame can prefer civics field size over journey opponent counts (`contest_source`).
> 
> Heavy **schema/docs** updates in `int__analytics.yaml` and `m_analytics.yaml`; new Airbyte source entry for voter file filters.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 17fb7fbbf2af4b9df1fcf39d875b36b94afbdb91. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

diff --git a/dbt/project/models/intermediate/analytics/int__user_candidacy_profile.sql b/dbt/project/models/intermediate/analytics/int__user_candidacy_profile.sql
index 8ce7c83..9069211 100644
--- a/dbt/project/models/intermediate/analytics/int__user_candidacy_profile.sql
+++ b/dbt/project/models/intermediate/analytics/int__user_candidacy_profile.sql
@@ -366,6 +366,16 @@ select
     pr.primary_result as candidacy_primary_result,
     cc.general_election_date as candidacy_general_election_date,
     cc.general_election_result as candidacy_general_result,
+    -- The day the race was decided for this candidate. A primary loss ends it
+    -- at the primary, so anything measured "before the race" stops there.
+    case
+        when
+            cc.latest_stage_result = 'Lost'
+            and cc.latest_stage_reached like 'primary%'
+            and cc.primary_election_date is not null
+        then cc.primary_election_date
+        else a.election_date
+    end as candidacy_race_date,
     -- Never null. A user with no candidacy is neither running nor a
     -- non-filer, and a null would drop them out of a `where not` filter.
     coalesce(a.election_date >= current_date(), false) as is_still_running,
diff --git a/dbt/project/models/intermediate/analytics/int__user_feature_use.sql b/dbt/project/models/intermediate/analytics/int__user_feature_use.sql
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..6d36d11
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dbt/project/models/intermediate/analytics/int__user_feature_use.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,47 @@
+-- When each user first and last used each Win feature, and on how many days.
+-- One row per user per feature used.
+--
+-- Which events count as a feature lives in the win_feature_events seed, so
+-- every analysis asking "did they use AI help" reads the same answer. Dates
+-- rather than flags: each analysis applies its own cutoff (before the race,
+-- first 30 days, by month) to the same rows.
+--
+-- Staff acting for the candidate is not the candidate using Win; the marker
+-- exists from 2026-03-24, and earlier impersonated events cannot be told apart.
+{{ config(materialized="table") }}
+
+with
+    features as (
+        select feature, event_type as event_pattern, match_type, is_user_action
+        from {{ ref("win_feature_events") }}
+    ),
+
+    events as (
+        select try_cast(e.user_id as bigint) as user_id, e.event_type, e.event_time
+        from {{ ref("int__amplitude_events_classified") }} as e
+        where
+            try_cast(e.user_id as bigint) is not null
+            and e.event_time >= '{{ var("product_telemetry_start") }}'
+            and not coalesce(e.is_machine_emitted, false)
+            and coalesce(e.event_properties:impersonation::string, 'false') != 'true'
+    ),
+
+    matched as (
+        select e.user_id, f.feature, f.is_user_action, e.event_time
+        from events as e
+        inner join
+            features as f
+            on (f.match_type = 'exact' and e.event_type = f.event_pattern)
+            or (f.match_type = 'prefix' and startswith(e.event_type, f.event_pattern))
+    )
+
+select
+    user_id,
+    feature,
+    -- Constant per feature in the seed.
+    any_value(is_user_action) as is_user_action,
+    min(event_time) as first_used_at,
+    max(event_time) as last_used_at,
+    count(distinct date(event_time)) as use_days
+from matched
+group by user_id, feature
diff --git a/dbt/project/models/intermediate/analytics/int__user_outreach_audiences.sql b/dbt/project/models/intermediate/analytics/int__user_outreach_audiences.sql
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..d67bb84
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dbt/project/models/intermediate/analytics/int__user_outreach_audiences.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,29 @@
+-- The audience behind each Win outreach send that has one: how narrowly it was
+-- cut, whether the candidate built it, and the message sent to it. One row per
+-- gp-api outreach row with a saved audience.
+--
+-- Social posts carry no audience, so they never appear here.
+with
+    campaign_users as (
+        select id as campaign_id, user_id
+        from {{ ref("stg_airbyte_source__gp_api_db_campaign") }}
+        where not coalesce(is_demo, false)
+    )
+
+select
+    o.id as outreach_id,
+    cu.user_id,
+    o.campaignid as campaign_id,
+    o.outreach_type,
+    o.status,
+    coalesce(o.date, o.createdat) as send_at,
+    o.voter_file_filter_id,
+    coalesce(o.message, o.script) as message_text,
+    f.demographic_dimension_count,
+    -- An untouched recommended list is ours; the candidate built the rest.
+    f.recommended_intent is null or f.is_recommended_modified as is_own_audience
+from {{ ref("stg_airbyte_source__gp_api_db_outreach") }} as o
+inner join
+    {{ ref("stg_airbyte_source__gp_api_db_voter_file_filter") }} as f
+    on f.voter_file_filter_id = o.voter_file_filter_id
+inner join campaign_users as cu on cu.campaign_id = o.campaignid
diff --git a/dbt/project/models/marts/analytics/m_analytics.yaml b/dbt/project/models/marts/analytics/m_analytics.yaml
index d1f2714..62a5342 100644
--- a/dbt/project/models/marts/analytics/m_analytics.yaml
+++ b/dbt/project/models/marts/analytics/m_analytics.yaml
@@ -4150,3 +4150,205 @@ models:
       - dbt_utils.expression_is_true:
           arguments:
             expression: row_count = user_count
+  - name: win_election_frame
+    description: >
+      One row per Win user with a 2026 race: the race, its result, and what the
+      candidate did in the product before it. Built for the post-election
+      analysis, which reads nothing else, so every count it prints traces to a
+      flag here.
+
+      Behavior is cut off at race_date. A primary loser's race is the primary,
+      so they are measured up to it. Result columns are null until a result is
+      matched; has_result is the share of results in so far.
+
+      The "who is counted" flags are applied in this order: is_real_user,
+      is_confirmed, has_result, contest_status = 'contested',
+      incumbency_status = 'challenger'. Unknown contest or incumbency status is
+      kept as its own value rather than folded into either side.
+    columns:
+      - name: user_id
+        description: gp-api user. The candidacy is user_journey's, one per user.
+        data_tests:
+          - not_null
+          - unique
+      - name: race_date
+        description: >
+          The date the race was decided for this candidate: the primary for a
+          primary loss, else the election date. Every behavioral column stops
+          the day before.
+        data_tests:
+          - not_null
+      - name: is_real_user
+        description: Not staff, internal or demo-only.
+        data_tests:
+          - not_null
+      - name: is_confirmed
+        description: Legitimacy label is "6. confirmed", the corroboration gate used across Win reporting.
+      - name: has_result
+        description: A won or lost result is matched. The results coverage measure.
+      - name: contest_status
+        description: >-
+          contested, uncontested, or unknown when the race facts are missing. Taken from the race's
+          actual candidate list in win_race_field where it exists, since the journey's opponent count
+          misses real opponents in some races; the journey otherwise.
+        data_tests:
+          - not_null
+          - accepted_values:
+              arguments:
+                values: ["contested", "uncontested", "unknown"]
+      - name: contest_source
+        description: Where contest_status came from, race or journey; null when neither knows.
+        data_tests:
+          - accepted_values:
+              arguments:
+                values: ["race", "journey"]
+      - name: baseline_win_chance
+        description: The race's baseline_win_chance from win_race_field, when the race is in the civics mart.
+      - name: incumbency_status
+        description: incumbent, challenger, or unknown.
+        data_tests:
+          - not_null
+          - accepted_values:
+              arguments:
+                values: ["incumbent", "challenger", "unknown"]
+      - name: is_race_past
+        description: race_date is today or earlier. A past race without a result is a coverage gap, not a pending one.
+      - name: is_winner
+        description: True for won, false for lost, null with no result.
+      - name: is_primary_loss
+        description: Lost at the primary stage. Counted as a loss and also shown apart.
+      - name: is_self_signup
+        description: Marketing-sourced rather than sales-sourced.
+      - name: is_paid_source
+        description: HubSpot original source is paid search or paid social.
+      - name: months_signup_to_race
+        description: Lead time from signup to race_date.
+      - name: is_pro_before_race
+        description: Pro, upgraded before race_date.
+      - name: is_pro_3_months_out
+        description: Upgraded to Pro 90 or more days before race_date.
+      - name: is_activated_before_race
+        description: Activated before race_date, on the governed activation definition.
+      - name: is_power_user
+        description: The governed power user flag, measured to the election as it defines.
+      - name: used_plan_opposition_research
+        description: >
+          The plan generated an opposition research section. It fires on plan
+          generation, so it marks having a v2 plan, not reading the research.
+          Every used_* column reads the shared feature definitions in
+          user_feature_use, cut at race_date.
+      - name: used_ai_help
+        description: Used AI help before race_date.
+      - name: first_ai_help_date
+        description: First AI help use, any date, for before/after comparisons.
+      - name: active_days_last_12_weeks
+        description: Win active days in the 12 weeks before race_date.
+        data_tests:
+          - not_null
+      - name: reach_per_1000_voters
+        description: Recipients across sends before race_date per 1,000 voters in the district. Null without a voter count.
+      - name: send_weeks_last_8
+        description: Distinct weeks with a Win send in the 8 weeks before race_date.
+      - name: channels_used
+        description: Distinct named channels sent on before race_date. Unattributed sends do not count as a channel.
+      - name: did_send_to_own_segment
+        description: Sent to an audience the candidate built or changed, not an untouched recommended list.
+      - name: demographic_audiences
+        description: Distinct sent audiences that narrow on at least one demographic family.
+      - name: demographic_messages
+        description: Distinct message texts sent to those audiences.
+      - name: is_targeted_messaging
+        description: Two or more demographic audiences and two or more distinct messages to them.
+      - name: team_touches_before_race
+        description: Outbound HubSpot touches before race_date.
+      - name: had_team_meeting
+        description: A HubSpot meeting before race_date.
+      - name: built_at
+        description: When this table was built. Pin it beside any count.
+  - name: user_feature_use
+    description: >
+      When each user first and last used each Win feature, and on how many
+      days. One row per user per feature used. Which events make up a feature
+      is the win_feature_events seed, so every analysis reads one definition;
+      apply your own cutoff to the dates. Per-column meaning lives on
+      int__user_feature_use.
+    data_tests:
+      - dbt_utils.unique_combination_of_columns:
+          arguments:
+            combination_of_columns: [user_id, feature]
+    columns:
+      - name: user_id
+        data_tests:
+          - not_null
+      - name: feature
+        data_tests:
+          - not_null
+          - relationships:
+              arguments:
+                to: ref('win_feature_events')
+                field: feature
+  - name: win_race_field
+    description: >
+      Every candidate in every 2026 race where a Win user ran, users and not:
+      one row per candidacy-stage. For comparing Win users with the rest of
+      their own field and with the odds each race gave.
+
+      Context columns are knowable before the race and outside the product's
+      reach. prior_candidacies and prior_wins only see the history the civics
+      mart holds, which starts in 2024, so they undercount for long-serving
+      candidates. prior_race_margin needs vote counts for the office's last
+      race and is rarely available.
+    columns:
+      - name: gp_candidacy_stage_id
+        data_tests:
+          - not_null
+          - unique
+      - name: gp_election_stage_id
+        data_tests:
+          - not_null
+      - name: is_win_user
+        description: The candidacy matches a gp-api campaign.
+        data_tests:
+          - not_null
+      - name: user_id
+        description: The Win user, when is_win_user.
+      - name: candidates_in_race
+        description: Candidacies the civics mart holds for this stage.
+        data_tests:
+          - not_null
+      - name: seats_in_race
+        description: >-
+          Seats on offer. Some multi-seat races are recorded with one seat, so once a race is decided
+          this is at least its number of winners.
+        data_tests:
+          - not_null
+      - name: is_contested
+        description: More candidates than seats, or a recorded loss (civics can miss a race's other candidates).
+        data_tests:
+          - not_null
+      - name: baseline_win_chance
+        description: >-
+          seats_in_race divided by candidates, capped at 1. The win rate if seats went to candidates at
+          random. Null when civics is missing the race's opponents (a loss with no more candidates than seats).
+        data_tests:
+          - dbt_utils.accepted_range:
+              arguments:
+                min_value: 0
+                max_value: 1
+      - name: is_november_general
+        description: A November general-stage race, the on-cycle date with the highest turnout.
+      - name: prior_candidacies
+        description: The person's earlier candidacies in the civics mart, other than this one.
+      - name: prior_wins
+        description: How many of those earlier candidacies won a stage.
+      - name: prior_race_margin
+        description: >
+          The same office's most recent earlier race of the same stage type:
+          vote share of the last seat won minus the first seat lost. Null
+          without vote counts for that race.
+      - name: is_winner
+        description: Won this stage. Null until a result is matched.
+      - name: vote_share
+        description: Votes received over total votes cast in the stage, where both are known.
+      - name: built_at
+        description: When this table was built.

diff --git a/dbt/project/models/marts/analytics/win_election_frame.sql b/dbt/project/models/marts/analytics/win_election_frame.sql
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..0e74a18
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dbt/project/models/marts/analytics/win_election_frame.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,361 @@
+-- One row per Win candidate with a 2026 race: who they are, how the race went,
+-- and what they did in the product before it. The post-election analysis reads
+-- only this table, so every count it prints traces to a flag here.
+--
+-- Everything behavioral is cut off at candidacy_race_date, the primary date for
+-- a primary loser. Feature and audience definitions come from the shared
+-- models; this table only picks the population and applies the cutoff.
+--
+-- The result columns stay null until a result is matched, so the same rows
+-- serve before, during and after results come in. has_result is the coverage
+-- measure.
+with
+    candidates as (
+        select
+            user_id,
+            candidacy_campaign_id as campaign_id,
+            candidacy_state as state,
+            candidacy_office as office,
+            candidacy_office_level_normalized as office_level,
+            candidacy_position_id as position_id,
+            candidacy_election_date as election_date,
+            candidacy_primary_election_date as primary_election_date,
+            candidacy_latest_stage_reached as latest_stage_reached,
+            candidacy_result,
+            candidacy_legitimacy_label as legitimacy_label,
+            candidacy_is_incumbent as is_incumbent,
+            candidacy_is_uncontested as is_uncontested,
+            candidacy_is_open_seat as is_open_seat,
+            candidacy_seats_available as seats_available,
+            candidacy_number_of_opponents as number_of_opponents,
+            candidacy_is_partisan as is_partisan,
+            candidacy_voter_count as voter_count,
+            candidacy_viability_score as viability_score,
+            candidacy_is_verified as is_verified,
+            registered_at,
+            acquisition_motion,
+            hs_analytics_source,
+            is_activated,
+            activated_at,
+            is_pro,
+            pro_since,
+            is_power_user,
+            onboarding_completed_at,
+            coalesce(is_internal, false)
+            or coalesce(is_demo_only, false) as is_staff_or_demo,
+            candidacy_race_date as race_date
+        from {{ ref("user_journey") }}
+        where has_candidacy and year(candidacy_election_date) = 2026
+    ),
+
+    -- Feature definitions are shared; this table only applies the race cutoff.
+    -- The race's actual candidate list, where civics has it. The journey's
+    -- opponent count misses real opponents in some races.
+    race as (
+        select
+            c.user_id,
+            bool_or(f.is_contested) as is_contested,
+            max(f.baseline_win_chance) as baseline_win_chance
+        from candidates as c
+        inner join
+            {{ ref("win_race_field") }} as f
+            on f.user_id = c.user_id
+            and f.election_date = c.race_date
+        group by c.user_id
+    ),
+
+    product_use as (
+        select
+            c.user_id,
+            coalesce(
+                bool_or(
+                    f.feature = 'onboarding_path_to_victory'
+                    and date(f.first_used_at) < c.race_date
+                ),
+                false
+            ) as used_onboarding_path_to_victory,
+            coalesce(
+                bool_or(
+                    f.feature = 'onboarding_v2' and date(f.first_used_at) < c.race_date
+                ),
+                false
+            ) as used_onboarding_v2,
+            coalesce(
+                bool_or(
+                    f.feature = 'plan_task' and date(f.first_used_at) < c.race_date
+                ),
+                false
+            ) as used_plan_task,
+            coalesce(
+                bool_or(
+                    f.feature = 'plan_opposition_research'
+                    and date(f.first_used_at) < c.race_date
+                ),
+                false
+            ) as used_plan_opposition_research,
+            coalesce(
+                bool_or(
+                    f.feature = 'story_rewrite' and date(f.first_used_at) < c.race_date
+                ),
+                false
+            ) as used_story_rewrite,
+            coalesce(
+                bool_or(
+                    f.feature = 'opponent_lookup'
+                    and date(f.first_used_at) < c.race_date
+                ),
+                false
+            ) as used_opponent_lookup,
+            coalesce(
+                bool_or(f.feature = 'ai_help' and date(f.first_used_at) < c.race_date),
+                false
+            ) as used_ai_help,
+            coalesce(
+                bool_or(
+                    f.feature = 'content_builder'
+                    and date(f.first_used_at) < c.race_date
+                ),
+                false
+            ) as used_content_builder,
+            coalesce(
+                bool_or(
+                    f.feature = 'segment_build' and date(f.first_used_at) < c.race_date
+                ),
+                false
+            ) as used_segment_build,
+            coalesce(
+                bool_or(
+                    f.feature = 'voter_file_download'
+                    and date(f.first_used_at) < c.race_date
+                ),
+                false
+            ) as used_voter_file_download,
+            coalesce(
+                bool_or(
+                    f.feature = 'team_invite' and date(f.first_used_at) < c.race_date
+                ),
+                false
+            ) as used_team_invite,
+            coalesce(
+                bool_or(
+                    f.feature = 'website_publish'
+                    and date(f.first_used_at) < c.race_date
+                ),
+                false
+            ) as used_website_publish,
+            coalesce(
+                bool_or(
+                    f.feature = 'profile_complete'
+                    and date(f.first_used_at) < c.race_date
+                ),
+                false
+            ) as used_profile_complete,
+            min(
+                case when f.feature = 'ai_help' then date(f.first_used_at) end
+            ) as first_ai_help_date,
+            min(
+                case when f.feature = 'opponent_lookup' then date(f.first_used_at) end
+            ) as first_opponent_lookup_date
+        from candidates as c
+        left join {{ ref("user_feature_use") }} as f on f.user_id = c.user_id
+        group by c.user_id
+    ),
+
+    sends as (
+        select s.user_id, s.channel, s.send_at, s.recipient_count
+        from {{ ref("int__user_outreach_sends") }} as s
+        where s.product = 'win'
+    ),
+
+    outreach as (
+        select
+            c.user_id,
+            count(s.send_at) as sends_before_race,
+            coalesce(sum(s.recipient_count), 0) as recipients_before_race,
+            count(
+                distinct case when s.channel != 'unattributed' then s.channel end
+            ) as channels_used,
+            count_if(s.channel = 'door_knocking') > 0 as did_door_knocking,
+            -- Weeks with a send in the final eight weeks.
+            count(
+                distinct case
+                    when date(s.send_at) >= date_sub(c.race_date, 56)
+                    then date_trunc('week', s.send_at)
+                end
+            ) as send_weeks_last_8
+        from candidates as c
+        left join sends as s on s.user_id = c.user_id and date(s.send_at) < c.race_date
+        group by c.user_id
+    ),
+
+    audience_sends as (
+        select
+            a.user_id,
+            a.voter_file_filter_id,
+            a.message_text,
+            a.demographic_dimension_count,
+            a.is_own_audience
+        from {{ ref("int__user_outreach_audiences") }} as a
+        inner join candidates as c on c.user_id = a.user_id
+        where a.status in ('completed', 'in_progress') and date(a.send_at) < c.race_date
+    ),
+
+    targeting as (
+        select
+            user_id,
+            count_if(is_own_audience) > 0 as did_send_to_own_segment,
+            count(
+                distinct case
+                    when demographic_dimension_count > 0 then voter_file_filter_id
+                end
+            ) as demographic_audiences,
+            count(
+                distinct case when demographic_dimension_count > 0 then message_text end
+            ) as demographic_messages,
+            max(demographic_dimension_count) as max_demographic_dimensions
+        from audience_sends
+        group by user_id
+    ),
+
+    activity as (
+        select
+            c.user_id,
+            coalesce(sum(w.win_activity_days), 0) as active_days_last_12_weeks
+        from candidates as c
+        left join
+            {{ ref("user_win_activity_weekly") }} as w
+            on w.user_id = c.user_id
+            and w.week_start_date >= date_sub(c.race_date, 84)
+            and w.week_start_date < c.race_date
+        group by c.user_id
+    ),
+
+    team_contact as (
+        select
+            c.user_id,
+            count_if(t.is_outbound_touch) as team_touches_before_race,
+            count_if(t.channel = 'meeting') > 0 as had_team_meeting,
+            min(
+                case when t.is_outbound_touch then date(t.touch_at) end
+            ) as first_team_touch_date
+        from candidates as c
+        left join
+            {{ ref("user_hubspot_touches") }} as t
+            on t.user_id = c.user_id
+            and date(t.touch_at) < c.race_date
+        group by c.user_id
+    )
+
+select
+    -- Keys and the race
+    c.user_id,
+    c.campaign_id,
+    c.state,
+    c.office,
+    c.office_level,
+    c.position_id,
+    c.election_date,
+    c.race_date,
+    c.latest_stage_reached,
+    c.seats_available,
+    c.number_of_opponents,
+    c.is_partisan,
+    c.voter_count,
+    c.viability_score,
+
+    -- Who is counted, in the order the report applies them
+    not c.is_staff_or_demo as is_real_user,
+    c.legitimacy_label = '6. confirmed' as is_confirmed,
+    c.candidacy_result in ('Won', 'Lost') as has_result,
+    case
+        when coalesce(r.is_contested, not c.is_uncontested)
+        then 'contested'
+        when not coalesce(r.is_contested, not c.is_uncontested)
+        then 'uncontested'
+        else 'unknown'
+    end as contest_status,
+    case
+        when r.is_contested is not null
+        then 'race'
+        when c.is_uncontested is not null
+        then 'journey'
+    end as contest_source,
+    r.baseline_win_chance,
+    case
+        when c.is_incumbent
+        then 'incumbent'
+        when not c.is_incumbent
+        then 'challenger'
+        else 'unknown'
+    end as incumbency_status,
+    c.race_date <= current_date() as is_race_past,
+
+    -- Outcome, null until matched
+    case
+        c.candidacy_result when 'Won' then true when 'Lost' then false
+    end as is_winner,
+    c.candidacy_result = 'Lost'
+    and c.latest_stage_reached like 'primary%' as is_primary_loss,
+
+    -- How they came and what they bought
+    c.registered_at,
+    c.acquisition_motion = 'marketing_sourced' as is_self_signup,
+    c.hs_analytics_source in ('PAID_SEARCH', 'PAID_SOCIAL') as is_paid_source,
+    months_between(c.race_date, date(c.registered_at)) as months_signup_to_race,
+    c.is_open_seat,
+    c.is_verified,
+    c.is_pro and date(c.pro_since) < c.race_date as is_pro_before_race,
+    coalesce(
+        date(c.pro_since) <= date_sub(c.race_date, 90), false
+    ) as is_pro_3_months_out,
+    c.is_activated and date(c.activated_at) < c.race_date as is_activated_before_race,
+    c.is_power_user,
+    date(c.onboarding_completed_at) < c.race_date as is_onboarded_before_race,
+
+    -- Product use before the race
+    p.used_onboarding_path_to_victory,
+    p.used_onboarding_v2,
+    p.used_plan_task,
+    p.used_plan_opposition_research,
+    p.used_story_rewrite,
+    p.used_opponent_lookup,
+    p.used_ai_help,
+    p.used_content_builder,
+    p.used_segment_build,
+    p.used_voter_file_download,
+    p.used_team_invite,
+    p.used_website_publish,
+    p.used_profile_complete,
+    p.first_ai_help_date,
+    p.first_opponent_lookup_date,
+    a.active_days_last_12_weeks,
+
+    -- Outreach before the race
+    o.sends_before_race,
+    o.recipients_before_race,
+    1000.0
+    * o.recipients_before_race
+    / nullif(c.voter_count, 0) as reach_per_1000_voters,
+    o.send_weeks_last_8,
+    o.channels_used,
+    o.did_door_knocking,
+    coalesce(t.did_send_to_own_segment, false) as did_send_to_own_segment,
+    coalesce(t.demographic_audiences, 0) as demographic_audiences,
+    coalesce(t.demographic_messages, 0) as demographic_messages,
+    coalesce(
+        t.demographic_audiences >= 2 and t.demographic_messages >= 2, false
+    ) as is_targeted_messaging,
+
+    -- Our team
+    tc.team_touches_before_race,
+    tc.had_team_meeting,
+    tc.first_team_touch_date,
+
+    current_timestamp() as built_at
+from candidates as c
+left join race as r on r.user_id = c.user_id
+left join product_use as p on p.user_id = c.user_id
+left join outreach as o on o.user_id = c.user_id
+left join targeting as t on t.user_id = c.user_id
+left join activity as a on a.user_id = c.user_id
+left join team_contact as tc on tc.user_id = c.user_id
diff --git a/dbt/project/models/marts/analytics/win_race_field.sql b/dbt/project/models/marts/analytics/win_race_field.sql
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..d8caeb9
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dbt/project/models/marts/analytics/win_race_field.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+-- Every candidate in every 2026 race where a Win user ran, users and not. One
+-- row per candidacy-stage. Lets the post-election analysis compare Win users
+-- with the rest of their own field, and set each result against the odds the
+-- race gave.
+--
+-- Context columns are all knowable before the race: incumbency, how often the
+-- person ran and won before, how close the same office's last race was, and
+-- election timing. Nothing here is something the product could influence.
+with
+    stages as (
+        select
+            gp_election_stage_id,
+            election_date,
+            stage_type,
+            is_primary,
+            is_runoff,
+            br_position_id,
+            office_level,
+            office_type,
+            partisan_type,
+            number_of_seats,
+            -- The civics mart carries vote counts as strings.
+            try_cast(total_votes_cast as bigint) as total_votes_cast
+        from {{ ref("election_stage") }}
+    ),
+
+    candidacy_stages as (
+        select
+            gp_candidacy_stage_id,
+            gp_candidacy_id,
+            gp_election_stage_id,
+            gp_person_id,
+            candidate_name,
+            candidate_party,
+            gp_api_campaign_id,
+            election_stage_date,
+            is_winner,
+            election_result,
+            try_cast(votes_received as bigint) as votes_received,
+            is_uncontested
+        from {{ ref("candidacy_stage") }}
+    ),
+
+    win_races as (
+        select distinct gp_election_stage_id
+        from candidacy_stages
+        where gp_api_campaign_id is not null and year(election_stage_date) = 2026
+    ),
+
+    campaign_users as (
+        select id as campaign_id, user_id
+        from {{ ref("stg_airbyte_source__gp_api_db_campaign") }}
+        where not coalesce(is_demo, false)
+    ),
+
+    candidacies as (
+        select gp_candidacy_id, is_incumbent, is_open_seat from {{ ref("candidacy") }}
+    ),
+
+    -- Each person's record before this stage, from every stage we hold.
+    person_history as (
+        select
+            cs.gp_candidacy_stage_id,
+            count(distinct prior.gp_candidacy_id) as prior_candidacies,
+            count(
+                distinct case when prior.is_winner then prior.gp_candidacy_id end
+            ) as prior_wins
+        from candidacy_stages as cs
+        inner join win_races as w on w.gp_election_stage_id = cs.gp_election_stage_id
+        left join
+            candidacy_stages as prior
+            on prior.gp_person_id = cs.gp_person_id
+            and prior.election_stage_date < cs.election_stage_date
+            -- Earlier stages of the same candidacy are this race, not a prior one.
+            and prior.gp_candidacy_id != cs.gp_candidacy_id
+        group by cs.gp_candidacy_stage_id
+    ),
+
+    -- The same office's most recent earlier race of the same stage type, and
+    -- how close it was: the gap in vote share between the last seat won and
+    -- the first seat lost.
+    prior_stage as (
+        select
+            s.gp_election_stage_id,
+            p.gp_election_stage_id as prior_election_stage_id,
+            p.number_of_seats as prior_seats,
+            p.total_votes_cast as prior_total_votes
+        from stages as s
+        inner join win_races as w on w.gp_election_stage_id = s.gp_election_stage_id
+        inner join
+            stages as p
+            on p.br_position_id = s.br_position_id
+            and p.stage_type = s.stage_type
+            and p.election_date < s.election_date
+        qualify
+            row_number() over (
+                partition by s.gp_election_stage_id order by p.election_date desc
+            )
+            = 1
+    ),
+
+    prior_ranked as (
+        select
+            ps.gp_election_stage_id,
+            ps.prior_seats,
+            cs.votes_received / nullif(ps.prior_total_votes, 0) as vote_share,
+            row_number() over (
+                partition by ps.gp_election_stage_id order by cs.votes_received desc
+            ) as finish
+        from prior_stage as ps
+        inner join
+            candidacy_stages as cs
+            on cs.gp_election_stage_id = ps.prior_election_stage_id
+        where cs.votes_received is not null
+    ),
+
+    prior_margin as (
+        select
+            gp_election_stage_id,
+            max(case when finish = coalesce(prior_seats, 1) then vote_share end) - max(
+                case when finish = coalesce(prior_seats, 1) + 1 then vote_share end
+            ) as prior_race_margin
+        from prior_ranked
+        group by gp_election_stage_id
+    ),
+
+    field_size as (
+        select
+            gp_election_stage_id,
+            count(*) as candidates_in_race,
+            count_if(is_winner) as winners_in_race,
+            count_if(not is_winner) as losers_in_race
+        from candidacy_stages
+        group by gp_election_stage_id
+    )
+
+select
+    cs.gp_candidacy_stage_id,
+    cs.gp_election_stage_id,
+    cs.gp_candidacy_id,
+    cs.gp_person_id,
+    cs.candidate_name,
+    cs.candidate_party,
+    cu.user_id,
+    cs.gp_api_campaign_id is not null as is_win_user,
+
+    -- The race
+    s.election_date,
+    s.stage_type,
+    s.is_primary,
+    s.is_runoff,
+    s.office_level,
+    s.office_type,
+    s.partisan_type,
+    s.number_of_seats,
+    fs.candidates_in_race,
+    -- Some multi-seat races are recorded with one seat. Once decided, the
+    -- winners show how many seats there were, a fact fixed before the vote.
+    greatest(coalesce(s.number_of_seats, 1), fs.winners_in_race) as seats_in_race,
+    -- A recorded loss means a contest even when civics is missing the opponents.
+    fs.candidates_in_race > seats_in_race or fs.losers_in_race > 0 as is_contested,
+    -- The share of candidates who win if seats were handed out at random.
+    -- Unknown when civics is missing opponents: a loss with no more
+    -- candidates than seats.
+    case
+        when fs.candidates_in_race > seats_in_race or fs.losers_in_race = 0
+        then least(seats_in_race / fs.candidates_in_race, 1.0)
+    end as baseline_win_chance,
+    -- On-cycle Novembers bring different turnout than off-cycle dates.
+    month(s.election_date) = 11 and not s.is_primary as is_november_general,
+    cs.is_uncontested,
+
+    -- The candidate, before the race
+    c.is_incumbent,
+    c.is_open_seat,
+    coalesce(ph.prior_candidacies, 0) as prior_candidacies,
+    coalesce(ph.prior_wins, 0) as prior_wins,
+    pm.prior_race_margin,
+
+    -- The result
+    cs.election_result,
+    cs.is_winner,
+    cs.votes_received,
+    cs.votes_received / nullif(s.total_votes_cast, 0) as vote_share,
+    current_timestamp() as built_at
+from candidacy_stages as cs
+inner join win_races as w on w.gp_election_stage_id = cs.gp_election_stage_id
+inner join stages as s on s.gp_election_stage_id = cs.gp_election_stage_id
+inner join field_size as fs on fs.gp_election_stage_id = cs.gp_election_stage_id
+left join campaign_users as cu on cu.campaign_id = cs.gp_api_campaign_id
+left join candidacies as c on c.gp_candidacy_id = cs.gp_candidacy_id
+left join person_history as ph on ph.gp_candidacy_stage_id = cs.gp_candidacy_stage_id
+left join prior_margin as pm on pm.gp_election_stage_id = cs.gp_election_stage_id

diff --git a/dbt/project/models/staging/airbyte_source/gp_api_db/stg_airbyte_source__gp_api_db_voter_file_filter.sql b/dbt/project/models/staging/airbyte_source/gp_api_db/stg_airbyte_source__gp_api_db_voter_file_filter.sql

index 0000000..c9a4ae8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dbt/project/models/staging/airbyte_source/gp_api_db/stg_airbyte_source__gp_api_db_voter_file_filter.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,108 @@
+{% set families = {
+    "age": [
+        "age_18_24",
+        "age_18_25",
+        "age_25_34",
+        "age_25_35",
+        "age_35_49",
+        "age_35_50",
+        "age_50_64",
+        "age_50_plus",
+        "age_65_plus",
+        "age_unknown",
+    ],
+    "gender": ["gender_male", "gender_female", "gender_unknown"],
+    "homeowner": [
+        "homeowner_yes",
+        "homeowner_likely",
+        "homeowner_no",
+        "homeowner_unknown",
+    ],
+    "education": [
+        "education_none",
+        "education_high_school_diploma",
+        "education_technical_school",
+        "education_some_college",
+        "education_college_degree",
+        "education_graduate_degree",
+        "education_unknown",
+    ],
+    "children": [
+        "has_children_yes",
+        "has_children_no",
+        "has_children_unknown",
+    ],
+    "marital": [
+        "married",
+        "single",
+        "likely_married",
+        "likely_single",
+        "marital_unknown",
+    ],
+    "ethnicity": [
+        "ethnicity_african_american",
+        "ethnicity_asian",
+        "ethnicity_european",
+        "ethnicity_hispanic",
+        "ethnicity_other",
+        "ethnicity_unknown",
+    ],
+    "veteran": ["veteran_yes", "veteran_unknown"],
+    "business_owner": ["business_owner_yes", "business_owner_unknown"],
+} %}
+-- The saved audience behind an outreach send, with the demographic choices that
+-- tell a targeted audience from a whole-district one. A family narrows the
+-- audience only when some but not all of its options are ticked: every age band
+-- ticked is the same audience as none. Each family counts once, so
+-- "homeowners, college degree" is two dimensions.
+with
+    source as (
+        select * from {{ source("airbyte_source", "gp_api_db_voter_file_filter") }}
+    ),
+
+    ticked as (
+        select
+            id as voter_file_filter_id,
+            name as filter_name,
+            created_at,
+            updated_at,
+            first_used_for_outreach_at,
+            recommended_intent,
+            coalesce(recommended_modified, false) as is_recommended_modified,
+            {%- for family, cols in families.items() %}
+                {% for col in cols -%}
+                    cast(coalesce({{ col }}, false) as int){{ " + " if not loop.last }}
+                {%- endfor %} as {{ family }}_ticked,
+            {%- endfor %}
+            coalesce(
+                size(from_json(income_ranges, 'array<string>')), 0
+            ) as income_ticked,
+            coalesce(
+                size(from_json(language_codes, 'array<string>')), 0
+            ) as language_ticked
+        from source
+    ),
+
+    flagged as (
+        select
+            * except (
+                {%- for family in families %}{{ family }}_ticked, {% endfor -%}
+                income_ticked,
+                language_ticked
+            ),
+            {%- for family, cols in families.items() %}
+                {{ family }}_ticked
+                between 1 and {{ cols | length - 1 }} as has_{{ family }}_filter,
+            {%- endfor %}
+            -- Nine income bands and four language options in the product.
+            income_ticked between 1 and 8 as has_income_filter,
+            language_ticked between 1 and 3 as has_language_filter
+        from ticked
+    )
+
+select
+    *,
+    {%- for family in families %} cast(has_{{ family }}_filter as int) + {%- endfor %}
+    cast(has_income_filter as int)
+    + cast(has_language_filter as int) as demographic_dimension_count
+from flagged

findings.body:
The upper bound `cols | length - 1` breaks the "every option ticked counts as no filter" rule for the `age` family. That family lists 10 columns, but they look like two overlapping sets of bands: `age_18_24`/`age_18_25`, `age_25_34`/`age_25_35`, `age_35_49`/`age_35_50`, `age_50_64`/`age_50_plus`. A user ticking every band in either version of the UI sets about 5–6 of the 10 columns, never 9 or 10. So `has_age_filter` comes out true for every audience with any age box ticked, including whole-district ones. That contradicts the model's own comment ("every age band ticked is the same audience as none") and overstates `demographic_dimension_count`, which feeds `demographic_audiences` and `is_targeted_messaging` in `win_election_frame`. Fix: give age its own "all ticked" check for each band set, or map the two sets onto one set before counting.

Falsification check: this is wrong if the two band sets are really one set of options shown together, or if an all-ticked audience stores all 10 columns as true. Nothing in the repo shows either, and I did not query `voter_file_filter` to confirm. Running `select age_18_24, age_18_25, count(*) ... group by 1,2` would settle it.

output.summary:
The PR adds the warehouse layer for the 2026 Win post-election report. It adds a `candidacy_race_date` that is cut at the primary for primary losers and reaches `user_journey` through `dbt_utils.star`. It also adds a `win_feature_events` seed with `int__user_feature_use`/`user_feature_use`, a staging model for `voter_file_filter` with demographic-narrowing counts, `int__user_outreach_audiences`, and the two marts `win_race_field` and `win_election_frame`. This matches the PR description.

The scout flagged nine areas, and deep-reviewers checked each one:
- **`win_race_field` arithmetic:** null `is_winner` before results arrive leaves `is_contested` and `baseline_win_chance` correct. The lateral `seats_in_race` alias doesn't collide with any upstream column, Databricks `/` returns a double, and `candidates_in_race` is never zero.
- **Joins and grain:** the frame's `race` join on `race_date` lines up with stage dates. Neither `win_race_field` nor `int__user_outreach_audiences` fans out, since the campaign, candidacy and filter keys are all tested unique.
- **Frame columns and tests:** `race_date` can't be null for rows that pass the 2026 filter. Every upstream column and literal the frame references exists ('6. confirmed', 'marketing_sourced', 'unattributed', 'door_knocking', 'meeting', 'win').
- **Shared feature definitions:** the impersonation check matches `int__user_engagement_days`, and `product_telemetry_start` is defined.

One problem holds up, posted inline: the `voter_file_filter` "all options ticked" threshold, where the overlapping age bands likely inflate the demographic dimension count.

Not verified here, so a human should confirm:
- Whether old- and new-schema age columns really coexist in the source.
- How `dbt seed` treats the trailing space in the `Onboarding V2 - ` prefix.
- The row counts quoted in the PR, checked against prod after the scheduled build picks up the new `user_journey` column.
